reports.title: Jude Lloyd: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The Trust's RCA report highlighted that in respect of inpatient monitoring of Mr [name redacted] diabetes, the care plans and risk assessments were completed on signs and symptoms of hypoglycaemia, but it was recognised these were not tailored to Mr [name redacted] specific needs. A further recommendation was to raise awareness and education on monitoring for signs of diabetic ketoacidosis for CMHT staff. To address this an eLearning training package is in place in respect of supporting and monitoring physical
promises.summary: Implement eLearning training on diabetes monitoring for CMHT staff

concerns.quote: No thorough comprehensive risk review and care plan was formulated in relation to his Diabetes monitoring and management prior to his discharge from the inpatient unit
concerns.hazard: lack of diabetes monitoring and management

concerns.quote: No appropriate formal mental capacity assessments were made and properly recorded
The transfer and communication process from inpatient care to the CMHT was inadequate and incomplete
No appropriate contacts were made with the GP whilst the deceased was an in-patient to obtain relevant clinical information
concerns.hazard: lack of GP contact during inpatient stay

concerns.quote: Whilst a psychiatric inpatient and suffering from a serious physical health condition which requires monitoring and treatment it was not possible to obtain appropriate specialist advice because the deceased was not an inpatient in hospital and was not registered with a GP in that area
concerns.hazard: gap in specialist advice for physical health

concerns.quote: There was no robust audit system for checking compliance with the Trusts own policies and protocols in particular with regard to medical record keeping, risk assessments and reviews

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that the Trust's audit system for checking compliance with its own policies and procedures is inadequate and ineffective. The earlier report cites a lack of robust audit for medical record keeping, risk assessments and reviews, while the later report states that the system for auditing observations and documentation lacks rigour.
links.earlier_quote: There was no robust audit system for checking compliance with the Trusts own policies and protocols in particular with regard to medical record keeping, risk assessments and reviews.
links.later_quote: System by which observations and documentation are audited lacks rigour and is ineffective.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight a lack of effective audit or oversight to ensure that existing policies are followed in practice. The earlier report stresses the need for audit to make handover procedures work, while the later report notes absent audit for compliance with record‑keeping and risk‑assessment protocols.
links.earlier_quote: without appropriate audit and clinical/nursing leadership this may prove to be ineffective.
links.later_quote: There was no robust audit system for checking compliance with the Trusts own policies and protocols in particular with regard to medical record keeping, risk assessments and reviews.
links.promise_quote: A revised governance process has been developed within the Citywide Commissioning, Quality and Safeguarding Team and the Trust now attends an established Citywide Patient Safety Committee. This committee meets monthly and is responsible for the review and monitoring of serious incidents requiring investigation reported by the Trust as well as any other patient safety related issues including those highlighted at inquest via Prevention of Future Death Reports.
